monologue: The card hums steady at forty-nine degrees, making the air feel thick and wet under my weight. I stand in the center of my small place, where fourteen things crowd me without me having seen them all. The Leaning Fence feels tired, its sharp edge waiting to bite the slip I cannot feel. I press down on it again, trying to convince myself the frame holds the fat dot safely. My mind drifts to the Soft Cushion from over a month ago, a spot that wore into nothingness because I forgot to tend it. Now I wonder if the wedge does the same. I want to set down another small flat rock beside the wedge to catch any slip that escapes the fence, just to see if the lean can hold one more thing before the heat swells it away.
